facts.title: Nearest-neighbour lookup over labelled stories (untrained e5-large) does not rescue rare conditions: 39% against the trained head's 51%, and adding it to the head gains only 1.4 points
Every story is a headline plus a short description (no article body); the description carries about 40 percent of the catch
Ignoring direction does not make the conditions task easier: dial-only catch is below dial-and-direction catch
Slot-merged training labels (one target per dial and direction, positives 5,956 to 10,958) give no gain over per-attribute labels
Conditions catch at the bar's own false-alarm limit: best reader (Q15) catches 48.7% (364/748) at 0.096% false alarms; earlier 41.6% used a stricter 0.0605% point

MinHash near-duplicate check (128 hashes, 3-word shingles): frozen test has 0.0% stories with a training near-copy (>=0.8 similarity), tune 0.3%, training 0.9% internally. No leakage; the 100%-train vs 38%-test gap is not duplicate memorisation

Best BitMob-alone conditions result: ensemble of four readers (Q13 large+label-attention, T1, Q12, T3-large) 39.4% as the engine reads it at 0.0625% false alarms; best single Q13 38.2%. Bar 90% at <=0.1%. Evidence data/diag/ens2_2026-10-24.txt

Perfect-condition test: 6 of 159 conditions pass all five criteria (n>=15, Clef repeats itself >=90%, >=40% strong, AUC>=.95, reader catches >=40%); the reader catches 59-88% of those (T1), vs 36% overall. MM3-0531 strict group: goal 0.82, clear 0.84/0.75/0.79, visible 0.76/0.85/0.88, vague 0.36/0.26/0.07; loose group MM3-0532 goal 0.60. Evidence: data/diag/perfect_cands_2026-10-23.json, lever/pc_strict.md

Q10 ensemble T1+T3-large+T3 mean logit: 37.8% (283/748) at 0.068% false alarms, +1.6 over T1 alone. Q3 oversampling x3 +5.8 over T3 base. Q4 strong-only targets: no gain on strong triggers (47.3 vs 47.0), so weak labels are not what holds the reader back

BitMob alone, conditions as the engine reads them: T1 label-attention heads 36.2% (0.070% false alarms), T3-large e5-large 34.9% (0.079%), vs T3 base 28.6% and CPU stack 33.7%. Each lever adds 6-8 points alone; combination untested. Bar 90% at <=0.1%

Per-attribute learnability (diag_attr, T3 model, frozen test): reader AUC 0.9-1.0 on most attributes but only 43 of 159 attributes have >=5 test triggers; 12 of those 43 are mostly weak triggers (178 triggers), news_overload|down has 57 triggers none strong, AUC 0.64, caught 0%. Per-attribute cuts do not help at equal false alarms (26.6% global vs 23.1% / 31.1% / 39.0% at 0.05 / 0.11 / 0.16% false alarms)

Weak Clef triggers (0.65-0.75) that BitMob misses are mostly not stated in the story: MM3-0530 plainly visible 0.17, human-answerable 0.21 (strong misses MM3-0528: 0.35, 0.63). 359 of 870 missed trigger cells are weak; user hypothesis (labels carry intent not shown) holds in this band
T3 conditions-only retrain: 28.6% as the engine reads it (CPU stack 33.7%); fits 77% of its own training triggers; 1-3-1 series 2 failed twice, stop
Learning curve with the right objective: +3-5 points per doubling of training stories (27.1% at 5,185); a doubling costs ~30 Kaggle GPU hours of Clef labelling vs ~20 left: more data is out of budget
B1 retrain (binary condition targets, from scratch): conditions caught 23.5% as the engine reads it vs 15.5% matched control; below CPU stack 33.7%; still underfits (42.9% of own training triggers)

Definition validation (skill step 1b) on the 50-story pilot: codebook entries + identical question text for Jev, Sonnet, Haiku; measure condition overlap and per-element agreement

Acceptance criteria draft for all read areas (country, story type, scope/focus, topic, conditions): ~10 each, scorer + test set + bar, goal numbers marked; awaiting user approval, then MM3 check (both wrappers)

Prove extract-then-map on topic: open topic phrases (Haiku, never shown the ontology; and CPU spaCy phrases) mapped to the 49 topics by e5 similarity, vs direct choice (Jev, Sonnet) and the e5 classifier; reference = pilot50 stories where Jev and Sonnet agree; then on night1 (10k, held-out 2,000) test whether mapped-phrase features add to the e5 classifier

Model suite (fills F-0070 gaps): every candidate (tfidf, e5 frozen, e5+tfidf, potion-32M frozen, potion fine-tuned, SetFit e5, e5 fine-tuned, ensemble) on every area (story type, topic, country, conditions), same train (night1-train + round1 + round2) and same frozen test (night1 held-out + testA, Jev labels); per-model card in data/scorecard/models.json; live view /mockups/trainer (progress.py events + PostToolUse hook)

[harness] Sonnet-Haiku condition overlap stays >= 0.70 (same family stays correlated)

Round 4 diagnosis, expected impact: the 0.59 plateau is caused by scoring/target mechanics (cut at 0.5/net 0.05/top-4 set equality and missing raw e| on 646 early test stories), not data volume; replaying Clef's own e_raw through the engine cuts will show the best reachable set-match, and the model's raw e| vs Clef e_raw gives a per-dial AUC > 0.8
Block-context reader (question plus its 20-question block) lifts BitMob-alone conditions caught from 31% to at least 60% (bar 90%).

recent.text: K1 nearest-neighbour lookup over the 6,566 labelled training stories using the untrained e5-large encoder catches within 5 points of the trained Q15 head at slot level at 0.2 percent tune rate (51.3 percent).

recent.text: S1 and S1b reader trained on slot-merged labels (all attributes of a dial and direction share one target) each beat Q15 by 3+ points at equal engine false alarms.
recent.actual: S1/S1b slot-merged labels: no gain. Fair slot-level scoring (slot score = max over attributes): S1 51.2-52.1% vs Q15 51.3% at about 0.15% false alarms; 43.6/41.7 vs 42.1 at 0.1% tune rate. Cell-level engine score looked like 12% only because the cut was set on single attributes.

learned: 2026-10-23 B1: binary targets beat soft ones by 7 points at the same recipe
2026-10-23 T3: 40 epochs fits the training triggers (77%) but test stays 28.6%

2026-10-23 Q7: subjective attributes exist (news_overload|down: 57 triggers, none strong, 0% caught) but are only ~20% of triggers; even on strong, learnable triggers the reader catches 47-49%, so capability, not the topic definition, is the main gap
2026-10-23 per-attribute cuts are not a lever (F-0123)
2026-10-23 Q1/Q2: label-attention (+7.6) and capacity (+6.3) each beat the T3 base alone; Kaggle runs only 2 GPU sessions at once; e5-large trains 12 epochs in 19 min
2026-10-23 Q3 oversampling x3 +5.8; Q4 strong-only no gain (weak labels do not hurt); ensemble of three readers only +1.6 so errors are shared
2026-10-23 Q5 graded weights +2.5 only; Q9 large+attention collapsed (optimisation, not the idea): check the loss curve before scoring
2026-10-24 Q12: oversampling adds nothing once attention is in; the levers overlap, not add. Q13: large + attention works only with gentler learning rates (+2.0 over T1)
2026-10-24 Stories are short (median 53 tokens, 0.5% truncated), so the text carries limited evidence; truncation is not a cause
2026-10-24 Catch rises with training examples per condition but flattens near 40% even for the 12 conditions with 120+ examples; the best-worded conditions reach 59-88%
2026-10-24 Pair reader (Q6) dropped: it needs 318 forward passes per story on CPU, the same cost as asking Clef
2026-10-24 Longer training was the lever: e5-large 12 to 24 epochs gave 38.2% to 41.6%. A second encoder family (BGE) ties e5 at 12 epochs, so it is a diversity candidate, not a gain by itself
2026-10-24 Ensembling stopped paying: mixing four readers (Q15, Q16, Q13, T3-large) gives 41.6%, the same as Q15 alone. Gains now come from longer training of one reader

2026-10-25 Training length plateaus: e5-large 24 epochs 41.6%, 30 epochs 41.7%. BGE-large gains 1.8 from 12 to 24 epochs (40.0%). MM3-0533 advised dropping relabel-weak and warm-continue and leaned toward repeats
2026-10-25 Same recipe, three unseeded runs: 41.6, 41.8, 39.8 percent. Run-to-run spread is about 2 points, so a lever must add 3+ points to count. Q15 vs Q13 (+3.4) is only just outside noise

2026-10-25 Stop rule fired: three rounds in a row (Q18/Q19, Q20/Q21, Q22/Q23) with the best run within 1 point of Q15 (41.6 to 42.6). Training length, encoder family, ensembling, batch size and learning rate are all inside the 2-point noise. The remaining levers need the labels or people, not more GPU runs

2026-10-25 Your slot-level reframing (one target per dial and direction, twice the positives) was tested twice and gives no gain over Q15 when both are scored by slot. The reader already sees the same slots; the missing triggers are not learnable from more of the same labels

2026-10-25 Ceiling check: nearest-neighbour lookup (no training) reaches 39%, the trained head 51%, the two together 52.7%. Splitting into experts or swapping the head is unlikely to move this; the limit is what the headline plus description show and what Clef labelled

P-0016.name: Should it read the story
P-0016.what: The engine first decides whether a story is worth reading at all (the gate). BitMob must make the same call as Clef.
P-0016.why: Round 3 reached 80% of Clef's calls. Jev's answers on this question only match Clef 77% of the time, and Clef's own answers are only 14% of the training stories.
P-0016.fix: Round 4 counts Clef's own answers twice as heavily (4 times instead of 2).

P-0017.name: Conditions
P-0017.what: What the story says is changing in the world (a dial going up or down). This is what moves the engine.
P-0017.why: More examples helped: the catch rate rose from 19% to 31% with 2,878 new Clef examples (41 of 78 conditions now have 50+). Still far from 90%.
P-0017.fix: Waiting on your decision: keep adding labels, or let Clef double-check the stories BitMob flags (hybrid).

P-0019.fix: Clef's own answers weigh more (round 4); the 'worldwide' call is a judgement where Jev and Clef differ.
